law_name: Act 332/2016 amending the Aliens Act (ulkomaalaislaki): repeal of humanitarian protection (HE 2/2016)
description: Government bill presented on 4 February 2016 by the Sipilä government while Orpo was Minister of the Interior. It repealed the provisions under which residence permits could be granted on grounds of humanitarian protection, leaving refugee status and subsidiary protection. The act entered into force on 16 May 2016.
significance: One of the main legislative responses to the 2015 rise in asylum applications in Finland.

law_name: Industrial peace legislation: amendments to the Collective Agreements Act and the Act on Mediation in Labour Disputes (HE 12/2024; Act 247/2024 and related acts)
description: Caps political strikes at 24 hours, restricts 'disproportionate' sympathy action and raises the compensatory fine for unlawful industrial action to between €10,000 and €150,000. Parliament passed it on 8 May 2024 by 107 votes to 57 (Centre and Movement Now joining the government parties); it entered into force on 18 May 2024.
significance: Prompted the union strike wave of September 2023–April 2024; the first of the government's labour-market reforms.

law_name: Act 482/2024 on temporary measures to combat instrumentalised migration (laki väliaikaisista toimenpiteistä välineellistetyn maahantulon torjumiseksi, HE 53/2024)
description: Allows the government to restrict, in a limited area and for a limited time, the receipt of asylum applications at the border when a foreign state is judged to be using migrants to put pressure on Finland. Passed on 12 July 2024 by 167 votes to 31, a five-sixths majority being required because it derogates from constitutional provisions; in force from 22 July 2024 and extended to 31 December 2026 by Act 368/2025 (HE 18/2025). A further government bill on the act (HE 148/2026) is pending.
significance: Criticised by the UNHCR; international law professor Martti Koskenniemi told Yle it was highly unlikely ever to be applied.

law_name: Amendments to the Citizenship Act (kansalaisuuslaki): Acts 474/2024, 929/2025 and 552/2026
description: Act 474/2024 (HE 27/2024, in force 1 October 2024) raised the general residence requirement for naturalisation from five to eight years and counts only time spent with a residence permit. Act 929/2025 (in force 17 December 2025) revised further conditions including the livelihood requirement, and Act 552/2026 adds a requirement to show sufficient knowledge of Finnish society in Finnish or Swedish from 1 January 2027.
significance: Implements the government programme's three-stage tightening of citizenship rules.

law_name: Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) between Finland and the United States
description: Negotiated by the Orpo government and approved unanimously by Parliament on 1 July 2024 (no vote was held because a motion to reject it received no support). It opens 15 Finnish military sites to potential use by US forces and allows the US to bring equipment, supplies and troops to Finland; Finnish law prohibiting nuclear weapons on Finnish soil is unaffected.
significance: Creates a framework for a more permanent US presence in Finland; negotiations began after Finland applied for NATO membership in May 2022.

law_name: Increase of the general VAT rate from 24% to 25.5%
description: Decided in the April 2024 budget framework talks and applied from 1 September 2024; the government expected more than €1 billion a year of extra revenue. The reduced 14% rate on food and restaurant meals and the 10% rate on medicines, accommodation, books and culture were left unchanged at the time.
significance: Among the largest single revenue measures of the term; a Statistics Finland report cited by Yle found it weighs disproportionately on lower-income earners.

law_name: Act 816/2024 amending the Act on Mediation in Labour Disputes: export-led wage model (HE 146/2024)
description: Government bill presented on 3 October 2024; prevents the National Conciliator from proposing settlements with wage increases above those agreed in the export sector. The opposition filed a joint no-confidence motion over it. In force from 1 January 2025.
significance: Applied in the 2025 bargaining round, led by the technology-industry agreement (7.8% over three years).

law_name: Legislation promoting local bargaining (HE 85/2024; Act 942/2024 amending the Employment Contracts Act and related acts)
description: Lets workplaces without union-organised employers apply the local-bargaining clauses of generally binding collective agreements, widening the scope for workplace-level agreements. In force from 1 January 2025.
significance: One of the labour-market reforms opposed by the unions in the 2023–2024 strike wave.

law_name: Amendments to the Basic Education Act and related acts restricting pupils' use of mobile devices
description: Approved by Parliament on 29 April 2025 and applied from August 2025. Pupils may use phones during lessons only with a teacher's permission (for example for study or health reasons), and staff may confiscate devices that disrupt teaching.
significance: Implements a commitment of the 2023 government programme to strengthen teachers' powers against disruption.

law_name: Withdrawal from the Ottawa Convention banning anti-personnel landmines
description: Announced by the government in spring 2025, approved by Parliament on 19 June 2025 by 157 votes to 18 (Left Alliance and Greens MPs and one SPP MP against); Finland deposited its denunciation on 10 July 2025 and the withdrawal took effect on 10 January 2026, allowing Finland to reintroduce anti-personnel mines.
significance: Taken in parallel with Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland on security grounds; Finland had been the last EU state to join the treaty, in 2012.

law_name: 2025 mid-term tax package: corporate tax cut to 18% and income-tax cuts
description: Agreed in the budget framework announced on 23 April 2025: income tax cuts for low- and middle-income earners (€525 million in 2026, €650 million in 2027), a higher employment income credit for parents, a top marginal rate of 52% for incomes above €100,000, the corporate tax rate cut from 20% to 18% from 2027, and VAT on food cut by half a point. The 2027 budget agreed on 1 September 2026 confirms the corporate tax cut.
significance: Yle reported criticism from economists and opposition parties that the cuts mostly benefit higher earners and would worsen debt; Orpo argued that growth would offset them.

description: Lowers the threshold for dismissing an employee on personal grounds: a 'proper reason' (asiallinen syy) suffices instead of a 'proper and weighty reason'. Approved on 19 December 2025 by 108 votes to 54 with 21 abstentions; in force from 1 January 2026.
significance: Called a 'firing law' by the opposition; the government presented it as helping small and medium-sized companies hire.

law_name: Act 48/2026 on the general benefit (laki yleistuesta, HE 112/2025)
description: Replaces Kela's labour market subsidy and basic unemployment allowance with a single means-tested 'general benefit' (yleistuki) for unemployed jobseekers, at the existing level (€37.21 a day in 2025). Given on 16 January 2026 and in force from 1 May 2026.
significance: Presented by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health as the first stage of a broader reform merging basic benefits into one universal benefit.

law_name: Act 412/2026 amending the Employment Contracts Act: fixed-term contracts (HE 199/2025)
description: Employers no longer need to justify offering a fixed-term rather than a permanent contract, and may terminate an employee's first fixed-term contract with them if it lasts up to one year. Approved on 20 May 2026 by 93 votes to 78; in force from 1 June 2026.
significance: Unions and women's groups raised concerns about discrimination against pregnant workers and employees planning parental leave.
